content.comment_body: Hello, Is it possible to use a [company_name] [product_name] relay output PLC with a [article_no] output module in the same setup? We have several installed on site in this configuration, with a relay module at the end. The transistor output module is only switching relay coils, but we are unable to get them to activate. Thank you, [user_name]
You can combine your [product_name] PLC with any expansion module that uses 12 VDC or 24 VDC power supply, but you cannot use it with expansion modules that require 230 VAC.

If you have a wiring diagram, please upload it—even a hand-drawn one could help. Make sure all modules have a supply voltage of 24V DC (L+ and M). All contact slides should be set correctly. Connect the transistor outputs (Qx) to the relay's positive side, and relay's negative side to M from the supply voltage, or M at the [product_name] module. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are discussing compatibility issues between a [company_name] relay output PLC and a transistor output expansion module, specifically when used to activate external relay coils. The main concern is that the relays are not energizing as expected. Responses are focused on checking voltage compatibility and wiring setup, indicating possible confusion or misunderstanding about configuring these modules together.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the relay output PLC and the output module to work together without issues, ensuring reliable activation of external relays. They want clear information regarding wiring and module compatibility.
